## Purpose

This SOP describes the extraction of inorganic nitrogen (nitrate,
NO~3~^-^, and ammonium, NH~4~^+^) from soil using 2 M potassium
chloride (KCl). The KCl extraction is the standard method for
determining plant-available inorganic nitrogen in soils
[@keeney1982; @mulvaney1996]. The high ionic strength of the KCl
solution displaces NH~4~^+^ from cation exchange sites and brings
NO~3~^-^ into solution, producing a filtered extract suitable for
colorimetric, flow-injection, or ion chromatographic analysis
[@maynard2008].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Field-moist or air-dried soil samples collected per
  [SOP-F400 Soil Sampling and Processing](../field_sops/SOP-F400-soil-sampling.qmd)
- **Does not apply to:** Total nitrogen analysis (requires Kjeldahl or
  combustion digestion; see [SOP-L407](SOP-L407-total-carbon.qmd));
  dissolved nitrogen in water samples; semi-quantitative field
  screening (see [SOP-L404](SOP-L404-nitrate-quick-test.qmd))
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## Responsibilities

## Definitions

- **Ammonium (NH~4~^+^):** The protonated form of ammonia; held on negatively charged cation exchange sites in soil; released into solution by the high ionic strength of the 2 M KCl extractant; the primary plant-available nitrogen pool in many soils.
- **Cation exchange capacity (CEC):** The total capacity of a soil to hold exchangeable positively charged ions; controls how much NH~4~^+^ can be stored and released; higher in clay-rich and organic-matter-rich soils.
- **KCl extraction:** Shaking soil with 2 mol L^-1^ potassium chloride solution at a defined soil-to-solution ratio (typically 1:10 w/v); the standard procedure for quantifying plant-available inorganic nitrogen in soils [@keeney1982].
- **Mineral nitrogen (mineral N):** The sum of NH~4~^+^-N and NO~3~^-^-N in the soil; the immediately plant-available nitrogen pool; expressed in mg N kg^-1^ dry soil.
- **Nitrate (NO~3~^-^):** The oxidized form of inorganic nitrogen; anion, so not held on cation exchange sites; highly mobile in soil solution; measured colorimetrically or by flow injection analysis after KCl extraction.
- **Soil-to-solution ratio:** The mass of soil (g) to volume of extractant (mL) used in the extraction; typically 1:10 for KCl extractions; must be consistent within and between studies for results to be comparable.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** 2 M KCl is a mild irritant; avoid contact with eyes
  and skin. Review the SDS before first use.
- **Physical:** Reciprocating shaker can pinch fingers if containers
  are not secured properly.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes

## Procedure

### Preparing 2 M KCl Solution

The 2 M KCl concentration is the standard for inorganic N extraction
[@keeney1982; @mulvaney1996]. Lower concentrations (e.g., 1 M) may
underestimate exchangeable NH~4~^+^ in high-CEC soils
[@maynard2008].

1. Weigh out 298.2 g KCl into a 2 L volumetric flask
2. Fill the flask approximately two-thirds full with distilled water
3. Place the flask on a magnetic stirrer and add a magnetic stir bar
4. Set the stirrer to low-medium speed and leave on for 4 hours until
   fully dissolved
5. Use a stir bar retriever to remove the magnetic stir bar
6. Fill the flask to the 2 L mark with distilled water and mix

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
Prepare the KCl solution the day before extraction. It can be stored
at room temperature in a capped container indefinitely. Verify the
solution with a conductivity meter if stored for more than 6 months.
:::

### Moisture Subsample

A companion gravimetric moisture determination is required to express
results on an oven-dry soil basis [@keeney1982].

1. Set aside 10 g of soil from each sample for moisture determination
2. Place each 10 g subsample into a labeled aluminum weigh boat
3. Dry at 105 C for 24 hours and record the dry weight
4. Calculate gravimetric moisture content per
   [SOP-L400 Soil Moisture](SOP-L400-soil-moisture.qmd)

### KCl Extraction

The standard soil-to-solution ratio is approximately 1:5 to 1:10
(w/v) [@mulvaney1996]. This SOP uses 7 g field-moist soil in 40 mL
KCl, yielding an effective ratio of approximately 1:6 on an oven-dry
basis for a typical soil at 15% gravimetric moisture.

1. Dispense 40 mL of 2 M KCl solution into labeled test tubes or
   extraction bottles
2. Add 7 g of field-moist soil to each tube (the total volume should
   reach approximately 50 mL). Record the exact mass of soil added
   to the nearest 0.01 g.
3. Cap the tubes securely
4. Place on the reciprocating shaker for 2 hours
5. Remove from the shaker and either:
   - Allow soil particles to settle for approximately 10 minutes (do
     not exceed 1 hour), or
   - Centrifuge for 3 minutes at 9,000 rpm (see
     [SOP-L109: Sorvall ST8R Centrifuge](SOP-L109-sorvall-centrifuge.qmd))

::: {.callout-important}
Record the exact mass of field-moist soil added to each tube. This
value, together with the gravimetric moisture content, is needed to
calculate results on an oven-dry basis (see Appendix A).
:::

### Filtering

1. Set up filter funnels with Whatman #42 filter paper over labeled
   specimen containers or clean test tubes
2. Pour the settled or centrifuged solution into the funnels; do not
   fill above the filter paper line
3. Allow the solution to drain completely until only soil remains on
   the filter
4. Discard the used filter paper and soil

### Extract Storage

1. Cap the filtered extract containers
2. If analysis will be completed within 48 hours, store at 4 C
3. If analysis will be delayed beyond 48 hours, freeze the extracts
   at -20 C until analysis [@keeney1982]

::: {.callout-important}
Extracts should be analyzed as soon as possible. Prolonged storage,
even frozen, can alter NH~4~^+^ and NO~3~^-^ concentrations due to
microbial activity or chemical transformations [@maynard2008].
:::


## Calculations

### Converting Extract Concentration to Soil Concentration

The colorimetric or flow-injection analyzer reports the concentration
of NO~3~^-^-N or NH~4~^+^-N in the filtered extract (mg N/L). To
convert this to mg N per kg oven-dry soil (ppm):

$$
C_{\text{soil}} \;(\text{mg N kg}^{-1}) \;=\;
\frac{C_{\text{extract}} \;\times\; V_{\text{KCl}}}{m_{\text{dry}}}
$$

where:

- $C_{\text{extract}}$ = concentration in the filtered extract
  (mg N/L)
- $V_{\text{KCl}}$ = volume of KCl extractant added (L; typically
  0.040 L)
- $m_{\text{dry}}$ = oven-dry equivalent mass of soil extracted (kg),
  calculated as:

$$
m_{\text{dry}} \;=\;
\frac{m_{\text{moist}}}{1 + \theta_g}
$$

where $m_{\text{moist}}$ is the field-moist mass added (g, converted to
kg) and $\theta_g$ is the gravimetric moisture content expressed as a
decimal (g water / g oven-dry soil).

See Appendix A for a worked R code example.

### Soil Texture Correction Factor (Optional)

When using the semi-quantitative quick test ([SOP-L404](SOP-L404-nitrate-quick-test.qmd)),
a texture-based correction factor may be applied. For the quantitative
KCl extraction described here, no texture correction is needed because
the exact soil mass and moisture content are measured directly.

| Texture | Moist Soil Factor | Dry Soil Factor |
|:--------|:-----------------:|:---------------:|
| Sand    | 2.3               | 2.6             |
| Loam    | 2.0               | 2.5             |
| Clay    | 1.7               | 2.2             |

These factors are retained here for reference when comparing quick-test
results to KCl extraction results.


## Quality Control

- Include a reagent blank (KCl solution only, no soil) in each
  extraction batch. The blank should read below the method detection
  limit for both NO~3~^-^-N and NH~4~^+^-N.
- Run extraction duplicates for at least 10% of samples. Duplicate
  results should agree within 15% relative percent difference (RPD).
- Include a laboratory reference soil with known inorganic N content
  in each batch when available.
- Record the KCl solution preparation date and batch number.
- Verify that the analytical calibration curve for the colorimetric
  method has an $r^2 \geq 0.995$ before reporting results.
- Subtract the mean reagent blank concentration from all sample
  results if the blank reads above zero [@mulvaney1996].


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type              | Disposal Method                             |
|:------------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| KCl extracts            | Aqueous waste; drain with copious water if approved by EH&S, or collect for pickup |
| Used filter paper and soil | Standard trash                           |
| Unused KCl solution     | Drain with water (non-hazardous at this concentration) |

## Appendix A: Calculation of Soil NO~3~^-^-N and NH~4~^+^-N (R Code) {.appendix}

The following R code converts extract concentrations (mg N/L from the
colorimetric analyzer) to soil concentrations (mg N/kg oven-dry soil,
equivalent to ppm) for a batch of samples. It corrects for the exact
mass of field-moist soil added and the gravimetric moisture content of
each sample.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# ===========================================================================
# SOP-L403: KCl Extraction -- Convert extract concentration to soil ppm
# ===========================================================================

# ---- 1. Enter your data ---------------------------------------------------
# Replace the example values below with your actual data.
# Each vector must have the same length (one entry per sample).

sample_id <- c("S01", "S02", "S03", "S04", "S05")

# Mass of field-moist soil added to the extraction tube (g)
soil_moist_g <- c(7.03, 7.10, 6.98, 7.05, 7.12)

# Gravimetric moisture content (proportion, g water / g oven-dry soil)
# From SOP-L400.  Example: 0.15 means 15% moisture.
theta_g <- c(0.152, 0.148, 0.161, 0.155, 0.143)

# Volume of 2 M KCl added (mL) -- typically 40 mL for all samples
vol_kcl_mL <- rep(40, length(sample_id))

# Extract concentrations from the colorimetric analyzer (mg N / L)
no3_extract_mg_L <- c(3.42, 5.18, 2.76, 4.01, 6.33)
nh4_extract_mg_L <- c(1.05, 0.87, 1.22, 0.93, 0.78)

# Reagent blank concentrations (mg N / L) -- mean of your blanks
blank_no3_mg_L <- 0.02
blank_nh4_mg_L <- 0.01

# ---- 2. Calculate oven-dry soil mass (kg) ----------------------------------
soil_dry_g  <- soil_moist_g / (1 + theta_g)
soil_dry_kg <- soil_dry_g / 1000

# ---- 3. Blank-correct extract concentrations --------------------------------
no3_corrected <- no3_extract_mg_L - blank_no3_mg_L
nh4_corrected <- nh4_extract_mg_L - blank_nh4_mg_L

# Ensure no negative values after blank correction
no3_corrected[no3_corrected < 0] <- 0
nh4_corrected[nh4_corrected < 0] <- 0

# ---- 4. Convert to mg N / kg oven-dry soil (ppm) ----------------------------
vol_kcl_L <- vol_kcl_mL / 1000

no3_ppm <- (no3_corrected * vol_kcl_L) / soil_dry_kg
nh4_ppm <- (nh4_corrected * vol_kcl_L) / soil_dry_kg

# ---- 5. Assemble results table -----------------------------------------------
results <- data.frame(
  Sample        = sample_id,
  Moist_g       = soil_moist_g,
  Moisture_pct  = round(theta_g * 100, 1),
  Dry_g         = round(soil_dry_g, 3),
  Vol_KCl_mL    = vol_kcl_mL,
  NO3_extract   = no3_extract_mg_L,
  NH4_extract   = nh4_extract_mg_L,
  NO3_ppm       = round(no3_ppm, 2),
  NH4_ppm       = round(nh4_ppm, 2),
  Total_inorgN  = round(no3_ppm + nh4_ppm, 2)
)

# ---- 6. Print results --------------------------------------------------------
cat("SOP-L403: KCl Extraction Results\n")
cat("================================\n\n")
print(results, row.names = FALSE)
cat("\n")
cat(sprintf("Reagent blank NO3-N: %.2f mg/L\n", blank_no3_mg_L))
cat(sprintf("Reagent blank NH4-N: %.2f mg/L\n", blank_nh4_mg_L))
cat("\nAll soil concentrations are mg N / kg oven-dry soil (ppm).\n")
```
:::


### Worked Example (Sample S01)

Using the example data above for sample S01:

- Field-moist soil added: 7.03 g
- Gravimetric moisture: 15.2% (0.152)
- Oven-dry equivalent: $7.03 / (1 + 0.152) = 6.102$ g = 0.006102 kg
- KCl volume: 40 mL = 0.040 L
- NO~3~^-^-N in extract: 3.42 mg/L (blank-corrected: 3.40 mg/L)
- Soil NO~3~^-^-N: $(3.40 \times 0.040) / 0.006102 = 22.29$ mg N/kg
  (ppm)
- NH~4~^+^-N in extract: 1.05 mg/L (blank-corrected: 1.04 mg/L)
- Soil NH~4~^+^-N: $(1.04 \times 0.040) / 0.006102 = 6.82$ mg N/kg
  (ppm)
- Total inorganic N: $22.29 + 6.82 = 29.11$ mg N/kg (ppm)


## Appendix B: Interpretation Guide {.appendix}

General interpretation thresholds for extractable inorganic N in
agricultural and wildland soils. These are approximate and vary by
crop, climate, and soil type [@hart1994; @mulvaney1996].

| Extractable Inorganic N (mg N/kg) | Interpretation      | Notes                                    |
|:----------------------------------|:--------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Less than 10                      | Low                 | Nitrogen likely limiting plant growth    |
| 10--25                            | Moderate            | Adequate for many crops and native vegetation |
| 25--50                            | High                | Sufficient N; fertilization generally not needed |
| Greater than 50                   | Very high           | Excess N; potential leaching or denitrification concern |
